question: What is the main goal of Maternal and Child Health (MCH) services?

options.A: To provide free surgical procedures for aging populations
options.B: To reduce preventable illness and death in mothers and children
options.C: To manage chronic diseases in older adults
options.D: To replace traditional birth practices completely

explanation: You got this! MCH services are specially designed to protect and support the health and survival of mothers and young children. Every win starts with knowing your core goal! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h1)

question: Why do we focus more on prevention than cure in MCH programs?

options.A: Preventive care stops complications before they become life-threatening
options.B: Curative care requires expensive machinery that is always unavailable
options.C: Curative care is prohibited in primary health care clinics
options.D: Preventive care completely eliminates the need for any medications

explanation: Spot-on! Stopping an illness before it takes root saves lives and energy compared to fighting an advanced disease later on. Prevention is your best tool as a nurse. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h1)

question: Which injection is routinely given during antenatal care to protect the newborn from tetanus?
explanation: Wonderful! Giving the tetanus toxoid vaccine to pregnant women helps build immunity that passes straight to the baby, keeping neonatal tetanus away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h2)

question: Why must pregnant women attend antenatal clinics even when they feel completely fine?

options.A: Pregnant women are legally required to visit the clinic every single week
options.B: It is impossible to eat a balanced diet without clinic supervision
options.C: Clinics require attendance records to secure international funding
options.D: Dangerous conditions like high blood pressure can develop without early warning signs

explanation: Exactly! Silent issues like pre-eclampsia or anemia can build up inside without any obvious signs at first. Routine checks keep both mum and baby safe. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h2)

question: When is the best time to put a newborn baby to the breast for the very first time?

options.A: Only when the mother's milk turns white
options.C: Within the first hour after birth

explanation: You nailed it! Starting breastfeeding within that first hour helps boost milk flow and gives the baby that precious, protective colostrum. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h3)

question: A new mother looks pale, feels dizzy, and her pad is soaked with bright red blood within 20 minutes. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Assess the uterine fundus for tone and massage if boggy
options.B: Wait until the scheduled six-week postnatal checkup
options.C: Tell the mother to walk around the room to improve circulation
options.D: Encourage the mother to drink large volumes of cold water

explanation: Great clinical thinking! These are classic signs of postpartum hemorrhage. Checking and massaging the uterus helps it contract and stops the bleeding. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h3)

question: What is the main reason for plotting a child's weight on a growth chart during clinic visits?

options.A: To check if the child needs immediate dental surgery
options.B: To calculate the exact adult height of the child
options.C: To determine how much money the family earns
options.D: To detect faltering growth early before severe malnutrition develops

explanation: Spot on! Growth charts let us catch weight drops or slow growth early so we can step in long before severe malnutrition sets in. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h4)

question: Why do nurses track developmental milestones like sitting up and walking in toddlers?

options.A: It determines when the child can stop receiving immunizations
options.B: It proves the child will excel academically in primary school
options.C: Milestones are only used for research and have no clinical value
options.D: Delays can signal underlying neurological, nutritional, or systemic problems

explanation: You got it! Tracking milestones helps you spot delays early so the child can get the right medical help or therapy quickly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h4)

question: Why is maintaining the cold chain so important in immunization programs?

options.A: To keep vaccines potent and effective until administration
options.B: To prevent the clinic refrigerator from overheating
options.C: To freeze liquid vaccines into solid blocks
options.D: To make the vaccines easier to draw into a syringe

explanation: Brilliant! Vaccines are delicate biological products. If they get too warm, they lose their power to protect children against diseases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a goal of the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI)?

options.A: Reducing childhood mortality rates across the country
options.B: Protecting infants from vaccine-preventable infectious diseases
options.C: Completely eliminating all chronic genetic disorders in children
options.D: Building community immunity against dangerous pathogens

explanation: Correct! EPI focuses on infectious, vaccine-preventable diseases. Genetic disorders are inherited and aren't targeted by standard immunization vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h5)

question: What is the main advantage of using the IMCI strategy when treating sick children?

options.A: It looks at the whole child and evaluates multiple overlapping symptoms
options.B: It focuses exclusively on treating severe surgical emergencies
options.C: It replaces the need for any laboratory testing in rural clinics
options.D: It removes the need for nurses to talk with caregivers

explanation: You're doing great! IMCI helps you assess the whole child because sick kids often suffer from more than one issue at the same time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h6)

question: A mother brings in her infant who is very sleepy (lethargic) and vomiting everything she feeds her. According to IMCI, what do these signs mean?

options.A: Normal infant behavior during a mild growth spurt
options.B: Minor symptoms that can be treated at home with rest
options.C: Side effects of routine immunization that need no action
options.D: General danger signs requiring urgent hospital referral

explanation: Spot on! Lethargy and inability to keep fluids down are red-flag danger signs. They mean the baby needs emergency hospital care right away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h6)

question: What is the recommended minimum time gap between pregnancies to protect mum and baby?
explanation: Wonderful! Waiting at least two years lets the mother recover her strength and nutrient stores, giving the next baby a healthier start. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h7)

question: Why is a mother's nutrition directly linked to her baby's health?

options.A: Nutritional deficiencies only affect the mother's hair and skin
options.B: Poor maternal nutrition often results in low birth weight and developmental challenges
options.C: Infants do not depend on maternal nutrient stores during pregnancy
options.D: A mother's diet has no effect on the fetus once the placenta forms

explanation: Exactly! The growing baby relies entirely on the mother for building blocks, making good maternal nutrition vital for proper growth. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h7)

question: What is a major role of Community Health Workers in maternal and child health?

options.A: Replacing professional nurses entirely in district hospitals
options.B: Conducting household visits and referring clients with danger signs to clinics
options.C: Importing foreign medical equipment for government clinics
options.D: Performing complex major surgeries in rural health posts

explanation: You got it! Community health workers bridge the gap by visiting homes, sharing health tips, and sending anyone with danger signs straight to the clinic. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h8)

question: Why is it important to involve traditional leaders and local birth attendants in primary health care?

options.A: They hold significant influence over community beliefs and healthcare-seeking behaviors
options.B: They are responsible for funding all primary health care clinics
options.C: They possess advanced medical degrees recognized by the nursing council
options.D: They act as legal inspectors of government health budgets

explanation: Brilliant! When respected local leaders are on board, community members are much more likely to trust nurses and use clinic services. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h8)
